correctness.rationale: The asserted asymptotic is mathematically valid under the explicitly uniform Maddux/Koussas formula: Q(n,n−2k)−Q(n,n)=−k(n−1), P(n,n−2k)=(n−2k−1)!k!2^k. Hence R_{n,k}=(n−1)!/[(n−2k−1)!k!2^k]·2^{−k(n−1)}, k<=floor((n−1)/2). The successive ratio is (n−2k−1)(n−2k−2)/[(k+1)2^n]; bounding it by n²/2^(n+1) controls tail/R_{n,1}=O(n²2^(−n)). R_{n,1}=(n−1)(n−2)/2^n, yielding both overall probability and conditional one-pair concentration. Uniform relative error is essential and present in the source. Fresh exact rational checks for n=7,10,15 corroborate the quotient and tail but do not validate the external asymptotic theorem.
